title: The night America set off a nuke in space ☢️
subject: aurora
description:
Would you have watched from the rooftop? 👇

In July 1962, the US detonated Starfish Prime, a 1.4-megaton hydrogen bomb, 400 km above the Pacific. Honolulu saw an artificial aurora, its streetlights failed, and a man-made radiation belt crippled satellites for months.

Sources: Wikipedia ("Starfish Prime", "Telstar 1", "High-altitude nuclear explosion"), Smithsonian Magazine ("Going Nuclear Over the Pacific"), APS News ("Sixty Years After, Physicists Model Electromagnetic Pulse of a Once-Secret Nuclear Test", 2022), Scientific American ("What Happens if a Nuclear Weapon Goes Off in Space?")

scenes.text: At 11 p.m., the sky over Honolulu turned red.
In July 1962, the US had exploded a 1.4-megaton bomb 400 kilometers above the Pacific.
It was launched from Johnston Island, about 1,450 kilometers away.
The pulse still reached Hawaii. About 300 streetlights went out and burglar alarms went off across Honolulu.
High above, the blast left a new radiation belt around Earth.
Within months, it crippled about a third of the satellites in low orbit, including Telstar 1.
